"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1126 -- a "sibilant + a + k-sound" word detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the piece of a word that
completes the spelling s/z + a + k-sound (c, k, ch, x), as in German "Sache"
(Tats|ache, S|ache, Haupts|ache), "Sachs", "Sack", "Sax", "sake" (for the sake of),
"Sak-", "tussac", "namesake". Typical values are around -5 on those tokens and near 0
everywhere else. The rule is written over the text: the word typed so far (lowercased,
since the last space) is checked, and the prediction is given only on the token where the
pattern first appears, so that "sache" counts once, not again on later pieces. The
lookahead drops "sac" before r/i/n/t/e (sacred, sacrifice, transact, transaction) and
"ch" before e/i, which the component does not respond to on average.

Known misses: a plain "a + k" with no s/z before it (ac, ak, act, axon) is only weakly
negative on average and is left at 0; Cyrillic "зак" and some other s/z-less k-sound
words are missed. Positive responses (e.g. "php", "ARR") are small and not modelled.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# s or z, then a, then a k-sound: c (not before r, i, n, t, e), k, ch (not before e, i), or x.
SAK_WORD = re.compile(r"[sz][aä](c(?![rinte])|k|ch(?![ei])|x)")

# The strength of the negative response on the completing token.
STRENGTH = -5.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[t]
    before = ""
    if t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        before = prefix.text_prefixes[t - 1]
    word = re.split(r"\s", text)[-1].lower()
    word_before = re.split(r"\s", before)[-1].lower()
    completes = SAK_WORD.search(word) is not None and SAK_WORD.search(word_before) is None
    return carry, (STRENGTH if completes else 0.0)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 1127: an indentation detector.

Fires on the whitespace that opens the body of a code line, when the line starts with
a gutter marker instead of a real line break:

  * a line number:       "   242<TAB>        code"   or  "    83      by ("
  * a diff/grep mark:    "+        code", "420-   code", "//<TAB> code", "|  cell"
  * an escaped newline:  "...;\\n    yield"            (backslash-n inside a string)

Value: a tab-led indent after a gutter grows with its width (about 1.2 for 4 columns,
saturating near 2.5). A spaces-only indent after a gutter is weaker (about 1.0).
Indent after an escaped newline is about 1.3. Indent right after a real newline stays 0,
and so do spaces inside prose.

Weaker triggers: the third digit of a year, the "1" or "2" in "201x" / "202x"
(about 1.4), and the NUL byte between letters of UTF-16-style text (about 1.3).

Carry: the text since the last real line break (capped), reset at each document start.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# text before an indent on a numbered, diff or grep-style line: a number (optionally
# followed by - or :), or a run of + - | : / marks, then an optional tab
GUTTER = re.compile(r"[ \t]*(?:\d+[-:]?|[-+|:/]+)\t?")
ESCAPED_NEWLINE = re.compile(r"\\n\Z")   # text so far ends in a literal backslash-n
YEAR_PREFIX = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)20\Z")  # text so far ends in "20" (not part of a longer number)


def _is_indent(s):
    # a run of spaces, tabs or no-break spaces, with no line break in it
    return s != "" and "\n" not in s and "\r" not in s and s.strip(" \t\xa0") == ""


def _width(s):
    # indent width in columns, tabs counted as 4
    return len(s.replace("\xa0", " ").expandtabs(4))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        carry = None  # a new document starts here: forget the text before it
    before = carry or ""
    line = before.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1]  # text since the last real line break

    value = 0.0
    if _is_indent(cur) and GUTTER.fullmatch(line):
        # indent right after a line-number or diff gutter
        if "\t" in cur:
            value = min(2.5, 1.0 + 0.1 * _width(cur))
        else:
            value = 1.0
    elif _is_indent(cur) and ESCAPED_NEWLINE.search(before):
        # indent right after an escaped newline inside a string
        value = 1.3
    elif cur in ("1", "2") and YEAR_PREFIX.search(before[-10:]):
        # third digit of a year: 201x or 202x
        value = 1.4
    elif cur == "\x00":
        # the zero byte between letters of UTF-16-style text ("h\x00a\x00t")
        value = 1.3

    if "\n" in cur:
        carry = cur.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1]
    else:
        carry = (before + cur)[-24:]
    return carry, float(value)

programs.sol:
"""A response to English possessive-looking phrases.

Join subword pieces into the current word-so-far.  Near a possessive,
body parts and words for personal existence get positive responses;
correspondence adjectives and some external social relations get negative
ones.  A small echo survives an intervening word.  Also recognize the
reverse construction, as in 'the minds of'.  These are semantic classes,
not a token-ID lookup; polysemy and noun-specific strengths are approximated.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
POSSESSIVES = frozenset((
    "my your his her its our their thy whose 's ’s ' ’"
).split())
SELF_CENTRES = frozenset('head heart mind soul'.split())
EXISTENCE = frozenset('life identity existence livelihood'.split())
WORK = frozenset(
    'job work career occupation profession duty responsibility task'.split()
)
# Spatial/structural words have anatomical senses in WordNet, but we do
# not treat their bare forms as names of body parts.
SPATIAL = frozenset((
    'right left side center centre system area form structure axis '
    'root column wall channel front middle bottom'
).split())
WORDS = re.compile(r"['’]s|(?<=[sS])['’]|[A-Za-z]+")
WORD_END = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z]+$')

FRESH = {
    'body_part': 1.52, 'life': 5.05, 'self_centres': 3.65,
    'correspondence': -6.15, 'business': 2.73, 'voice': 3.09,
    'personal_label': 1.91, 'mouth': 4.13, 'potential': 1.39,
    'people': -0.24, 'home': 1.13, 'work': 0.83,
    'breath': 2.80, 'geographic': -1.58, 'adversary': -1.12,
}
AFTER_ONE_WORD = {'existence': 2.51, 'self_centres': 3.37, 'in': -0.48}


@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def meanings(word):
    if not word.isalpha():
        return {}
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun'))
    categories = wordnet.categories(word, 'noun')
    body = (len(word) >= 3 and not bases & SPATIAL
            and wordnet.is_a(word, 'body part'))
    return {
        'body_part': body,
        'life': 'life' in bases,
        'self_centres': bool(bases & SELF_CENTRES),
        'existence': bool(bases & EXISTENCE),
        'mouth': 'mouth' in bases,
        'personal_label': bool(bases & {'name', 'surname', 'nickname'}),
        'business': 'business' in bases,
        'voice': 'voice' in bases,
        'breath': 'breath' in bases,
        'work': bool(bases & WORK),
        'home': bool(bases & {'home', 'house', 'household'}),
        'potential': bool(bases & {'potential', 'capacity', 'ability', 'power'}),
        'correspondence': word in {'respective', 'corresponding'},
        'geographic': word in {
            'local', 'regional', 'national', 'international', 'global'
        },
        'people': ('noun.person' in categories and not body
                   and not bases & (EXISTENCE | SELF_CENTRES)),
        'adversary': wordnet.is_a(word, 'adversary'),
        'in': word == 'in',
    }


def weighted(weights, features):
    return sum(weight * features.get(name, 0.0)
               for name, weight in weights.items())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    old = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (old + token)[-160:]
    tail = WORD_END.search(text)
    if tail and token[-1:].isalpha():
        word = tail.group().lower()
        before = text[:tail.start()]
    else:
        word, before = token.strip().lower(), old
    previous = WORDS.findall(before.lower())[-4:]
    near = [len(previous) >= n and previous[-n] in POSSESSIVES
            for n in (1, 2, 3)]
    reverse = word == 'of' and token.strip().lower() == 'of'
    value = 0.0
    if any(near) or reverse:
        features = meanings(word)
        if near[0]:
            value += weighted(FRESH, features)
        if near[1]:
            value += weighted(AFTER_ONE_WORD, features)
        if previous:
            prior = meanings(previous[-1])
            if word == 'to':
                value += 1.97 * prior.get('potential', 0.0)
            if reverse:
                value += 1.14 * prior.get('self_centres', 0.0)
    return (doc, text), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 1128: a possessive-noun rule.

What it does: it fires on the word right after a possessive ("my", "your", "his",
"her", "their", "our", "its", or "'s") when that word is a body part or a word for
one's own life, work or abilities: "my job", "their face", "our life", "your tongue",
"my livelihood". There it predicts a positive activation of 3.0; everywhere else, 0.

What it leaves out: after possessives that name people or outside things
("my men", "your competitor", "their neighbor"), the component is often strongly
negative, but a word list for those did not carry over to held-out text, so the
program predicts 0 there. Most of the component's variance is in these possessive
contexts, with mixed sign, so this rule captures only the positive half of it.
"""

READS = ()

POSSESSIVE = {"my", "your", "his", "her", "their", "our", "its", "'s"}

BODY_AND_LIFE = {
    "face", "hands", "hand", "fingers", "finger", "tongue", "teeth", "eyes", "eye",
    "head", "heart", "mouth", "lips", "body", "voice", "mind", "hair", "nose",
    "feet", "legs", "arms", "skin", "blood", "bones", "ears", "shoulders",
    "life", "livelihood", "job", "ability", "abilities", "health", "day",
    "identity", "possession", "work", "career",
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    if len(toks) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    prev = toks[-2].strip().lower()
    word = toks[-1].strip().lower()
    if prev in POSSESSIVE and word in BODY_AND_LIFE:
        return carry, VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on a single bare space token
(" ") that starts a line, i.e. the space that sits between a line break and the
indented text that follows, as in "\n  foo" tokenised as "\n", " ", " foo".
Inside code or escaped text, where a newline is written as the two characters
backslash-n, the same thing happens. In those cases the component's activation
is about -1.3 (real newline) or about -1.9 (escaped newline). On every other
token it is near zero, with small background wobble that has no simple rule.

Why: the model cannot see the next token, so the component fires on the context
where an indented word is likely to follow a bare space. It is negative
whenever that holds and near zero otherwise. The program covers only these two
cases and predicts 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

REAL_NEWLINE_SPACE = -1.27    # mean activation: " " right after a real line break
ESCAPED_NEWLINE_SPACE = -1.95  # mean activation: " " right after an escaped "\n"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if tokens[-1] == " " and same_doc:
        before = tokens[-2]
        if before.endswith("\n"):
            value = REAL_NEWLINE_SPACE
        elif before == "\\n" or (before == "n" and len(prefix) > 2 and tokens[-3].endswith("\\")):
            value = ESCAPED_NEWLINE_SPACE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 1130: a token-level detector.

Its activation depends mostly on which token is being read, not on its context:

- Strongly negative on Go's blank identifier `_` used as a discarded value, as in
  `for _, x := range` or `_, err := f()`. The bare token " _," is about -8.
- Negative on other empty or placeholder arguments that end in a comma or close a
  bracket: [], ?, "", {}, :, and on path fragments such as "./", "*.", "../".
- Mildly positive on Japanese particles, most strongly on の-compounds
  (のみ, のだ, のも, のは, のか), かも, だけ and という. Plain の, と, も, 了 and 的 are weakly positive.
- Everything else is about 0.

The program is a lookup on the current token alone, with no context. On about 8,000
training rows it explains about 0.2 of the variance, and about 0.29 on the eval rows.
Covering the long tail of rarer tokens needs a much larger table, and the rest of the
variance depends on context that this program does not model.

BLANK = {
    " _,": -8.0,
    "(_,": -6.5,
    " (_,": -6.0,
    " _:": -6.0,
    "_,": -1.7,
    "(_)": -3.7,
    "_)": -3.3,
    " _)": -4.5,
}

    "([],": -3.9,
    " ?,": -2.9,
    ' "",': -2.0,
    " {},": -1.7,
    " :,": -2.6,
    " *,": -2.4,
    " [],\n": -2.2,
    " ()": -0.8,

# Japanese and Chinese particles, positive.
PARTICLES = {
    "のみ": 2.1,
    "のだ": 1.8,
    "のも": 1.6,
    "のは": 1.2,
    "のか": 1.0,
    "のに": 1.1,
    "のが": 1.0,
    "かも": 1.3,

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 1131: a "honesty / humility / kindness" word detector.

What it does: the component is silent on almost all text, and lights up on the token that
completes a word of the honesty, humility or kindness family, e.g. " honest", "honestly",
"frankly", "dishonest", "humble", "humbled", "humbly", "kind" / "kindly" / "unkind", and Chinese
诚 / 真诚 / 诚信 (sincere), 忠诚 (loyal), 承诺 / 諾 (promise). "kind" gets one value in every
sense; the program does not tell the adjective ("your kind words") from the noun ("this kind
of"), though the noun is weaker in the data.

How: it keeps the letters of the current word (reset at any non-letter and at each new
document). A stem fires if it occurs in that word and ends inside the current token.
Chinese words are matched token by token. Everything else predicts 0.

Document start: the first token of each document has no earlier context, and its activation
depends only on the token: function words (the, of, and, is ...) are a little negative, and
digits and punctuation a little positive.

Scale: values are typical activations on the stems (from ~8000 training rows).
"""

# Stems of English words of the honesty / humility / kindness family, with a typical activation.
STEMS = {
    "honest": 2.4,  # honest, honesty, honestly, dishonest
    "frankly": 3.4,
    "humbl": 2.2,  # humble, humbly, humbled, humbles
    "truthful": 0.7,
    "sincerely": 0.9,
    "kind": 0.9,  # kind, kindly, kindness, unkind (any sense)
}
# Words that contain a stem but are not the family (kindle, kinder-garten, kindred ...).
NOT_STEM_WORDS = ("kindl", "kindred", "kinderg", "kinda")

# Chinese words for sincerity, loyalty and promise, matched as whole tokens.
ZH = {
    "诚": 5.7,
    "誠": 5.6,
    "真诚": 2.3,
    "诚信": 2.0,
    "忠诚": 1.9,
    "承诺": 2.6,
    "諾": 2.7,
    "诺": 1.0,
}

# Function words, and the document-start activation of each class.
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "the a an of and or in on at to is are was were be for with by from that this it as but not".split()
)
START_FUNCTION = -0.14
START_PUNCT_OR_DIGIT = 0.15

READS = ()


def stem_value(word, start):
    """The activation of the first stem found in `word` that ends after `start`."""
    if word.startswith(NOT_STEM_WORDS):
        return 0.0
    for stem, value in STEMS.items():
        i = word.find(stem)
        while i >= 0:
            if i + len(stem) > start:

            i = word.find(stem, i + 1)
    return 0.0

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    prev = "" if new_doc else carry

    word = prev
    for ch in tok:
        word = word + ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ""
    # A token made only of letters continues the previous word, so the stem must end past it.
    start = len(prev) if tok.isalpha() else 0
    value = stem_value(word, start)

    if value == 0.0 and new_doc:
        text = tok.strip().lower()
        if text in FUNCTION_WORDS:
            value = START_FUNCTION
        elif text.isdigit() or (text and text.isascii() and not text.isalnum()):
            value = START_PUNCT_OR_DIGIT
    return word, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1132: a "for" detector.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
- The English word "for" written as its own token (" for", "for", "\\tfor", " FOR").
  How strongly depends on the word just before it:
    * "for" opening a clause after a linking word ("that for all", "So for each",
      "But for the case", "then for")                             -> strong
    * "for" after a comma, "and" / "or", or a bracket or quote    -> medium
    * "for" at the start of a line or after indentation (code loops, "for i in")
                                                                  -> weak-medium
    * "for" as a preposition after a verb or noun ("looking for",
      "responsible for", "used for", "you for")                   -> about zero
- Capitalised sentence-initial "For" (" For", "For")             -> high
- Other spellings of the same sound: fort, ford, fork, forth, fore, för, fö,
  voor, für, фор                                                 -> high
- A word fragment that completes "for" spelled across two tokens after an
  "f" or "F" (f + ör, f + ors, F + ORT, F + ORD)                  -> high
- Everything else, including form, force, forward, forget, forum: zero.

The values are the average activation for each class, measured on training rows.
The program is stateless: it reads only the current token and the one before it,
and treats the first token of a document as if nothing came before it.
"""

READS = ()

LINKING_BEFORE = {"that", "so", "but", "then", "thus", "hence"}
CLAUSE_BEFORE = {"and", "or", ",", ".", ";", ":", "),", "(", '"'}
FOR_SPELLINGS = {"fort", "ford", "fork", "forth", "fore", "för", "fö", "voor", "für", "фор"}
SPLIT_ENDINGS = {"ör", "ors", "ö", "ort", "ord", "org", "ork", "orn", "orth", "ur", "ret", "ø", "rd"}


def activation(cur, prev):

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1133: a Hungarian word-fragment detector.

The component is silent on most text. Its large values sit inside Hungarian passages,
and there its sign follows the role of the current token inside a word:

* the first fragment of a word, when it is a piece of a word and not a whole function
  word (e.g. "el", "meg", "sz", "h" in "elterül", "megfelel", "szer..."): positive;
* a later fragment of a word that is a common Hungarian ending (-ág, -ban, -ott, -ok,
  -ik, -ás, -ó, -at, -ra ...): strongly negative;
* a later fragment that is not an ending (a root continuation): mildly positive, or
  mildly negative for the third and later fragments.

"Hungarian" is judged causally: the share of accented Hungarian letters
(á é í ó ö ő ú ü ű) among all letters so far in the document must be at least 0.1.
Everywhere else the prediction is 0.
"""

READS = ()

HU_ACCENTS = set("áéíóöőúüűÁÉÍÓÖŐÚÜŰ")
HU_THRESHOLD = 0.1
HU_ENDINGS = set("""ott ett ött ás és ok ek ök ak ág ég ban ben ik os es ó ő at et ít ál át ét
ól ol ul ül ja je ra re lt zt án ú ü ly i á""".split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = {"a", "és", "nem", "é"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        accents, letters, piece = 0, 0, -1
    else:
        accents, letters, piece = carry
    accents += sum(ch in HU_ACCENTS for ch in token)
    letters += sum(ch.isalpha() for ch in token)
    core = token.strip()
    if core.isalpha() and not token.startswith(" ") and piece >= 0:
        piece += 1          # the word goes on
    elif core.isalpha():
        piece = 0           # a new word starts
    else:
        piece = -1          # punctuation, digits, other scripts
    hungarian = letters > 0 and accents / letters >= HU_THRESHOLD
    if not hungarian or piece < 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif piece == 0:
        value = 0.0 if core in FUNCTION_WORDS else 0.6
    elif core in HU_ENDINGS:
        value = -0.9 if piece >= 2 else -0.3
    elif piece == 1:
        value = 0.5
    else:
        value = -0.2
    return (accents, letters, piece), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 1134: a "theme / topic" word detector.

It goes negative on the word-piece that completes a word for "theme" or "topic" in
many languages (theme, themes, Thema, tema, тема, テーマ, 主题, ...), more strongly on
Greek-root "box/library" words such as Bibliothek, Infothek, hydrotheca (theke/theca),
and weakly on -thesis words (antithesis, hypothesis). It is slightly positive on the
dot-leader token '··' and on " of" after "nothing", "something", "little".
Everything else predicts 0. Only the first piece that completes a root fires, so the
later pieces of the same word stay quiet.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()

THEME_WORDS = {"theme", "themes", "themed", "themen", "thema", "temas", "tema", "temi",
               "тема", "теме", "тему", "темы", "темой", "тематика", "тематики"}
THEME_CJK = ("主题", "主題", "テーマ", "話題", "課題")
BOX_ROOTS = ("thek", "theca", "thec", "theke")
THESIS_ROOTS = ("thesis", "thesi")
THEME_VALUE = -2.0
BOX_VALUE = -3.0
THESIS_VALUE = -0.5
CJK_VALUE = -1.0
DOT_VALUE = 1.2
OF_VALUE = 2.5


def _trailing_word(text):
    i = len(text)
    while i > 0 and unicodedata.category(text[i - 1])[0] in "LM":
        i -= 1
    return text[i:].lower()


def _completes(word, before, roots):
    """True if some root appears in `word` but not in the word before this token."""
    return any(r in word and r not in before for r in roots)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] == "··":
        return None, DOT_VALUE
    if any(text.endswith(w) for w in THEME_CJK):
        return None, CJK_VALUE
    word = _trailing_word(text)
    before = _trailing_word(prefix.text_prefixes[-2]) if len(prefix.text_prefixes) > 1 else ""
    if word in THEME_WORDS:
        return None, THEME_VALUE
    if _completes(word, before, BOX_ROOTS):
        return None, BOX_VALUE
    if _completes(word, before, THESIS_ROOTS):
        return None, THESIS_VALUE
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] == " of" and before in ("nothing", "something", "little"):
        return None, OF_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

Dictionary glosses match a property to an appropriate adjective: time can be
long, cost high, weight light, performance good, and so on. Bare adjectives

modifier. This shares gains across semantic classes, not individual word pairs.

    ('rate degree level density temperature price cost threshold interest index '
     'height standard quality', 'high low tall short'),
    ('time duration history distance length', 'long short'),

    ('speed pace reaction response', 'fast slow quick sensitive keen'),
    ('weight', 'heavy light'),
    ('performance quality taste flavor shape appearance',
     'good bad poor fine excellent reliable stable'),
    ('expression express explanation argument information',
     'clear distinct explicit transparent'),
    ('data evidence preparation prepare', 'ample sufficient adequate full'),
    ('knowledge erudition experience', 'wide broad extensive profound'),

    '啊 吧 呢 吗 么 也 都 就 又 还 再 很 更 最 太 不 没 没有 有 '
    '我 你 他 她 它 我们 你们 他们 她们 这个 那个 这 那 其 之 所 '
    '一个 可以 可能 会 到 来 去 上 下 中 内 外 前 后 '
    '以下 以上 以前 以后 之间 每次 一次 '

MODIFIERS = frozenset('不较較最很更太')

def meanings(text):
    """Content words in glosses, and simple adjectival glosses separately."""

        return frozenset(), frozenset()
    if len(text) > 1 and text[0] in MODIFIERS:
        text = text[1:]

    for gloss in cedict.glosses(text):
        for part in gloss.split(';'):
            part = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', part).strip().lower()
            if part.startswith(('surname ', 'cl:', 'variant ', 'see ')):
                continue

                words.add(token)
                words.update(wordnet.base_forms(token))
            simple = len(tokens) == 1 or re.fullmatch(r'[a-z]+-[a-z]+', part)

                    'adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(tokens[0])):
                adjectives.add(tokens[0])

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, count = '', 0
    else:
        _, previous, count = carry
    nouns, _ = meanings(previous)
    _, adjectives = meanings(text)
    value = -0.015 if adjectives else 0.0
    # Single characters are too ambiguous except standard property suffixes.
    named_property = len(previous) > 1 or previous in MEASUREMENT_SUFFIXES
    if named_property and any(nouns & n and adjectives & a for n, a in DIMENSIONS):
        modified = len(text) > 1 and text[0] in MODIFIERS
        value = -1.2 if modified else -4.3

        value = 0.62
    if count == 1 and previous == 'Title' and text == ':':
        value = 5.1
    if text == '··' and previous == '··':
        value = -0.817
    return (doc, text, count + 1), float(value)

- It is most negative when the adjective predicates a measurable attribute of the noun just

W_CONTEXT = -0.35  # adjective after a plain noun or a degree adverb

"""Approximate the component's Chinese counting and quantity responses.

Dictionary meanings identify classifiers, with separate strengths for people,
objects, items, sounds, brief bursts, and slender objects. A number or determiner
can precede the classifier within its token or in the previous text. Numerals,
demonstratives, and collective quantities also contribute; the whole-family
expression has a positive response. Recent Han prose strengthens predictions;
kana, Latin letters, and chat markup weaken them. Other tokens return zero.
The recent text and chat flag reset at document boundaries.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import cedict
from opencc import OpenCC

READS = ()
_simplify = OpenCC('t2s').convert
NUMERALS = '零〇一二三四五六七八九十百千万亿兆两半'
DETERMINERS = '这那某每各几多整另同本哪'
_QUANTITY = regex.compile('[' + NUMERALS + DETERMINERS + r'\d]\s*$')

@lru_cache(None)
def construction(token):
    s = _simplify(token.strip())
    if not s or not regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Han}+', s):
        return None
    if s == '一家':
        return 'family', False, False
    end = s[-1]
    glosses = cedict.glosses(end)
    classifiers = [g for g in glosses if g.startswith('classifier')]
    internal_count = len(s) > 1 and bool(_QUANTITY.search(s[:-1]))
    if end == '个' and len(s) > 1:
        internal_count = True
    if len(s) == 1 or internal_count:
        if any(g.startswith('classifier for people') for g in classifiers):
            honorific = any('honorific' in g for g in classifiers)
            kind = 'honorific' if honorific else 'person'
            if kind == 'person' and internal_count:
                kind = 'person_compound'
            return kind, internal_count, s.startswith('各')
        if end == '个':
            return 'object', internal_count, False
        if any('principles, items' in g for g in classifiers):
            return 'item', internal_count, False
        if classifiers:
            for fragment, kind in (('for sounds', 'sound'),
                                   ('short duration', 'burst'),
                                   ('long slender', 'slender')):
                if any(fragment in g for g in classifiers):
                    return kind, internal_count, False
            return 'measure', internal_count, False
    if s == '全体':
        return 'all_members', False, False
    if s in ('众', '诸'):
        return 'collective', False, False
    if s in ('这', '那', '此') or s.endswith(('在这', '在那')):
        return 'demonstrative', False, False
    number = s.removesuffix('美元').removesuffix('元')
    if number and all(c in NUMERALS for c in number):
        return ('large_number' if any(c in '千万亿兆' for c in number)
                else 'number'), False, False
    if any(g.startswith(('some', 'many', 'a little', 'a few', 'how much',
                         'number; amount', '(great) majority', 'whole; all'))
           for g in cedict.glosses(s)):
        return 'quantity', False, False
    return None

# Fitted magnitudes for recognizable Chinese constructions.
VALUES = {
    'all_members': -2.83,
    'burst_bare': -0.11,
    'burst_count': -0.87,
    'collective': -0.26,
    'demonstrative': -0.36,
    'family': 1.68,
    'honorific_bare': -0.41,
    'honorific_count': -2.42,
    'item_bare': -0.06,
    'item_count': -0.83,
    'large_number': -0.60,
    'measure_count': -0.14,
    'number': -0.06,
    'object_bare': -0.67,
    'object_count': -0.76,
    'person_bare': -0.65,
    'person_compound': -3.67,
    'person_count': -4.64,
    'quantity': -0.07,
    'slender_bare': -0.10,
    'slender_count': -1.14,
    'sound_count': -1.31,
    'vocative': -0.89,
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        past, chat = '', False
    else:
        _, past, chat = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    chat = chat or '<|im_start|>' in token
    c = construction(token)
    value = 0.0
    if c is not None:
        kind, counted, vocative = c
        if kind in ('person', 'honorific', 'object', 'item', 'measure',
                    'sound', 'burst', 'slender'):
            counted = counted or bool(_QUANTITY.search(_simplify(past[-8:])))
            kind += '_count' if counted else '_bare'
            if vocative:
                kind = 'vocative'
        han = len(regex.findall(r'\p{Han}', past))
        kana = len(regex.findall(r'[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]', past))
        latin = sum(ch.isascii() and ch.isalpha() for ch in past)
        density = han / max(10, han + kana + latin)
        gain = density * max(0.0, 1 - 2*kana/max(1, han+kana))
        gain *= 0.07 if chat else 1.0
        value = VALUES.get(kind, 0.0) * gain
    return (doc, (past + token)[-80:], chat), float(value)

Book, text, source, edition and publishing vocabulary produces negative values;
explanation/presentation vocabulary is mildly positive. A recent text word also
makes a following connecting preposition negative. 'Full', 'edited', 'collected',
etc. strengthen a text mention. Dictionary readings extend the same rules to
Chinese/Japanese. Citation/page-count rules and a small document-start offset
complete the predictor. State resets per document. Not all contextual variation
is captured.

import regex
import codecs
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
import cedict
import jmdict

TEXT_GROUPS = (
    (-.70, 'book textbook handbook guidebook workbook booklet paperback ebook'),
    (-.25, 'edition volume encyclopedia compendium'),
    (-.25, 'publication publish publishing print printing'),
    (-.20, 'reference bibliography citation source resource'),
    (-.40, 'supplement supplementary appendix annex addendum'),
    (-.45, 'version copy reproduction translation original'),
    (-.20, 'document report bulletin transcript transcription'),
    (-.30, 'novel poetry poem fiction nonfiction testament scripture bible gospel'),
    (-.10, 'chapter introduction preface prologue epilogue excerpt passage'),
    (-.25, 'text literature writings works'),
    (-.20, 'article essay journal paper manuscript dissertation thesis'),
    (-.35, 'author editor publisher coauthor'),
    (-.30, 'library archive collection anthology'),
    (-.20, 'guide manual tutorial primer'),
)
GROUPS = TEXT_GROUPS + (
    (+.16, 'explain describe demonstrate discuss show illustrate depict speaker narrator'),
    (-.20, 'comprehensive introductory'),
    (-.15, 'page leaf'),
    (-.10, 'cover title entitled'),
)
GROUPS = tuple((weight, frozenset(words.split())) for weight,words in GROUPS)
BOOK_NAMES = frozenset('livre livres libro libros libri livro livros buch bücher '
                       'книга книги книгу книг كتاب الكتاب 책'.split())
CONNECTORS = frozenset('of to in on by from with for'.split())
MODIFIERS = frozenset('full complete comprehensive introductory edited printed '
                      'collected memorial reference main'.split())

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def classes(word):
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    return frozenset(i for i,(_,words) in enumerate(GROUPS) if forms & words)

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def meaning(word):
    found = set(classes(word))
    if word in BOOK_NAMES or word.endswith(('book','books')):
        found.add(0)
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}',word):
        # An unspaced word can span tokens: use the longest recognized suffix.
        for n in range(1,min(4,len(word))+1):

            for gloss in cedict.glosses(word[-n:]) + jmdict.glosses(word[-n:]):

                if re.fullmatch(r'[a-z]+(?: [a-z]+){0,2}',gloss):
                    matches.update(classes(gloss))
            if matches:

                found = {min(matches)}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    _, tail, previous, recent, pending = (doc,'','',0.,b'') if start else carry
    raw = pending + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    token, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(raw,'ignore',False)
    pending = raw[used:]

    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+',joined)
    word = words[-1].lower() if words else ''
    value, text_word = meaning(word) if any(c.isalpha() for c in token) else (0.,False)
    if word in CONNECTORS:
        value -= .40*recent
    if text_word and previous in MODIFIERS:
        value -= .80
    if word in ('bib','bibl','ref','refs','ed','eds'):
        value -= .10
    if word in ('p','pp','page','pages') and previous.isdigit():
        value -= .20
    if start:
        value += .08
    recent = max(.7*recent,float(text_word))
    if any(c in token for c in '.!?\n'):
        recent *= .3
    if token.strip():
        previous = token.strip() if token.strip().isdigit() else word
    tail = words[-1][-40:] if words and joined[-1].isalpha() else ''
    return (doc,tail,previous,recent,pending),float(value)

        value = -0.4 if prev.endswith(BLOCK_ENDS) else -0.25
    elif starts_line and leading_space:
        value = -0.2
    elif cur == "··":
        value = -0.6
    elif cur in HEADINGS:
        value = -0.25
    elif cur == " RUN":
        value = -0.3
    elif cur == "\r" or cur == "#include":
        value = 0.2
    if value == 0.0 and first_of_document:
        value = -0.1
    return carry, value
